**OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra targets everyday computer use at half the API price.** The model is built for work such as filling out forms or entering invoice details into accounting software. OpenAI says it completes tasks over three times faster than GPT-6 Astra, at standard API prices 50% lower than GPT-5.6 Terra; the benchmarks are OpenAI's own. [OpenAI, 26 Oct 2026](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-terra/)

**OpenAI introduced "dots", always-on personal agents.** Dots are powered by GPT-6 Astra, have their own cloud computer, connect to over 4,000 apps through plugins, and can be reached through ChatGPT, Slack or Teams. Rollout starts on Pro, Business Premium and Enterprise plans in eligible markets, with action review and approvals among the stated controls. [OpenAI, 29 Sep 2026](https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/)

**IBM and OpenAI formed a consulting partnership.** Announced on 13 August, it embeds GPT-5.6, Codex and ChatGPT Work into IBM Consulting Advantage, IBM's delivery platform. IBM is also launching a dedicated OpenAI Practice with "thousands of consultants and engineers" and forward-deployed units working directly with clients. This is a vendor announcement. **OpenAI paused work on its next model, Astra, over cyber capabilities.** Less than a week after presenting Astra's scientific results, OpenAI said it "cannot rule out critical cyber capabilities" under its Preparedness Framework and was pausing internal activities on the model. Its previous high-end model, GPT-5.6 Sol, had only reached the "high" threshold. [PCWorld, 7 Aug 2026](https://www.pcworld.com/article/3208734/openai-pumps-the-brakes-on-new-astra-model-over-cybersecurity-concerns.html)
